name: Shortcuts App
description: Apple Shortcuts is a device automation app for combining actions from Apple and third-party apps into reusable workflows on Mac, iPhone, iPad and Apple Watch.
agentUseSummary: Shortcuts App is visible as a local-runtime security preview. Relay will not invoke mutable, name-selected workflows until the Mac bridge can bind an inspected shortcut version and enforce device-local approval and privacy boundaries.

capabilities.label: Run approved local shortcuts
capabilities.description: After local bridge hardening, run only an inspected and version-bound shortcut on the connected Mac within its Apple-granted privacy authority.

blocked.label: Run a shortcut from Railway
blocked.description: Apple exposes Shortcuts as device-local automation; Relay will not pretend a cloud API or route local private data through Railway.

blocked.label: Trust a mutable shortcut name
blocked.description: A shortcut's actions can change while its name remains the same, so name selection alone is not an immutable authority boundary.

blocked.label: Run unreviewed private or external actions
blocked.description: Shortcuts may access private device data, create or send items, open apps, post content and invoke third-party actions.

blocked.label: Run actions before local bridge hardening
blocked.description: No list, import, export, inspect or run action is callable until the device-local bridge enforces version binding, input/output bounds, prompts, auditing and revocation.

approvalProfiles.label: Local bridge review required
approvalProfiles.description: Connection, installation and execution remain unavailable until Relay can bind immutable shortcut content and enforce local privacy and approval controls.

runtimeSupport.description: No OpenClaw tool is callable until a hardened Mac-local bridge can bind and audit approved shortcut content.
No Hermes tool is callable until a hardened Mac-local bridge can bind and audit approved shortcut content.

providerSetup.blocker: Apple's supported CLI runs mutable device-local shortcuts by name; a shortcut can access private data or external apps and can change after selection without changing its name.
providerSetup.nextAction: Implement a Mac-local bridge that exports and hashes inspected shortcut content, binds the exact version and device, caps typed input/output, treats prompts as non-headless, requires approval for every external effect, audits locally, detects drift and revokes the binding on change.

evidence.supports: Apple documents running nearly any shortcut from the local command line with files or text as input and output, while interactive shortcuts pause awaiting user input.
Apple documents sequential execution, runtime prompts and explicit permission dialogs when a shortcut action needs private device data.
Apple documents per-shortcut privacy grants, Allow Once or Always Allow decisions, privacy reset, large-data sharing and warnings for untrusted shared shortcuts.
Apple documents Shortcuts actions that create items, save files, post content, open apps and invoke Apple or third-party integrations.
